items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: And from there I met Earl Klugh. And we became friends, and another saxophone player who still lives in the Detroit area, his name is Allan Burns, a tenor player.

ctx.x: I felt that somehow I wasn’t up to snuff to be considered to be able to do that. As much as I played, as much as I enjoyed it, I just felt that I didn’t have all that it takes to really be © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

in there. But he felt different. And I did my first major gig with Kenny Burrell in Detroit, at Baker’s Keyboard Lounge. And from there I met Earl Klugh. And we became friends, and another saxophone player who still lives in the Detroit area, his name is Allan Burns, a tenor player. So I was started to get slowly acclimated into this whole professional situation.
